questions.question: Which statement is the strongest core invariant for a regenerative AI claim?
options: Any efficient model is regenerative
Purchased offsets can replace lifecycle measurement
Own footprint, avoided impact, and external outcomes remain separately measured inside a declared boundary
A positive use case cancels the service footprint automatically
questions.explanation: Separate ledgers prevent unlike quantities and weak counterfactuals from being silently netted into one marketing number.

questions.question: An inference optimization cuts energy per request by 40%, but request volume doubles. What should the team conclude first?
options: Total operational energy is 40% lower
Total operational energy is 20% higher before other lifecycle terms
The system is carbon negative
Demand growth does not affect the footprint
questions.explanation: The new total is 0.60 x 2.00 = 1.20 times the baseline, demonstrating why intensity and absolute totals must both be tracked.

questions.question: Why choose a functional unit such as an accepted answer instead of a raw model call?
options: It guarantees two systems have identical quality
It removes the need to measure hardware
It converts all environmental outcomes into carbon
It ties impact to useful service delivered and exposes retries or discarded calls
questions.explanation: A useful functional unit makes intensity operationally meaningful while quality and lifecycle boundaries still require separate evidence.

questions.question: What does temporal carbon-aware scheduling change most directly?
options: The carbon intensity associated with when electricity is consumed
The embodied emissions already assigned to hardware
The causal effect of an environmental intervention
The model's accuracy by definition
questions.explanation: Time shifting can reduce operational emissions when the electricity mix is cleaner, but it does not erase energy demand or other lifecycle terms.

questions.question: Which evidence is required before saying an AI system caused an external environmental improvement?
options: A sustainability-themed product name
A lower cloud bill
A counterfactual baseline, measured outcome, attribution analysis, and monitoring for durability and leakage
A single model accuracy score
questions.explanation: External contribution claims depend on what would have happened otherwise and whether the observed improvement persists or shifts harm elsewhere.

questions.question: A model identifies 100 possible leaks. Which value is an outcome rather than an AI output?
options: The number of prediction rows emitted
Confirmed leaks repaired earlier because operators acted on the prioritization
The confidence score distribution
The number of GPUs used
questions.explanation: Predictions are intermediate outputs. The environmental outcome occurs only when the socio-technical system changes real-world action.

questions.question: Why allocate embodied hardware emissions to the service boundary?
options: Embodied emissions are always larger than operational emissions
The allocation makes offsets unnecessary
Hardware allocation proves causality for external benefits
Manufacturing and replacing hardware create impacts that operational electricity metrics omit
questions.explanation: Lifecycle accounting includes a defensible share of hardware impact; its magnitude depends on equipment, utilization, lifetime, and allocation method.

questions.question: Which release gate best limits rebound risk?
options: Track both impact per functional unit and the absolute monthly footprint with a demand budget
Track only cost per request
Hide total usage after an efficiency release
Assume lower latency means lower total impact
questions.explanation: Intensity can improve while total impact rises. A demand budget and absolute ledger make that divergence visible.
